# Lead Lab Web App Delivery Plan
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent) on behalf of Agno JF

**Recommendation:** Build a zero-license-cost, self-hosted MVP by September 10, 2026. Keep SharePoint available as the launch fallback until the new app passes acceptance testing.

**Plan Status:** Proposed  
**Target launch:** September 10, 2026  
**Current date:** August 19, 2026  
**Available delivery window:** 23 calendar days

## Product Goal

Create one private Lead Lab learning community inspired by Skool. It will combine community discussions, recorded sessions, materials, and events.

This is not a general community platform or an exact Skool clone.

## Launch Scope

| Area | Required capability |
|---|---|
| Access | Participant self-registration with a participant-only role, pending state, and administrator approval, revocation, and restoration; target-state email verification is required |
| Security | All community content blocked for unauthenticated users |
| Roles | Participant, moderator, and administrator |
| Community | Posts, comments, categories, pinned announcements |
| Classroom | Courses, modules, recorded sessions, materials, and an administrator recordings page reachable from dashboard Classroom navigation |
| Video | Embedded YouTube videos |
| Resources | Protected downloadable files |
| Discovery | Search plus category and date filters |
| Calendar | Events with dates, times, and descriptions |
| Administration | Manage members, posts, courses, lessons, files, and events |
| Devices | Responsive desktop, tablet, and mobile interface |

## Deferred Scope

- Payments and subscriptions
- Points and leaderboards
- Direct messaging
- Public community discovery
- Multiple communities
- Microsoft 365 SSO
- Native mobile applications
- Video hosting or streaming
- Advanced analytics
- Course completion certificates
- Automated marketing emails
- Existing SharePoint content migration

## Technical Plan

The server environment is not yet known. Environment verification is the first delivery gate.

### Default Stack

Use this stack if the existing server supports PHP and MySQL:

| Component | Selection |
|---|---|
| Application | Laravel modular monolith |
| Interface | Server-rendered responsive UI, optionally using Livewire |
| Database | Existing MySQL or MariaDB |
| Authentication | Laravel application-managed authentication with self-registration, configurable email verification, and administrator-controlled approval |
| Files | Private server storage outside the public web directory |
| Search | Database-backed search |
| Web server | Existing Apache or Nginx |
| Deployment | Existing IT server |
| Video | YouTube embeds |
| Cost | No software licence cost |

If PHP and MySQL are unavailable, IT should select the environment already supported by the team. The project should not introduce microservices or unfamiliar infrastructure.

### Core Data

- Users and roles
- Categories
- Community posts and comments
- Courses, modules, and lessons
- Lesson video links
- Resource files
- Events
- Administrative activity logs

The app will support one Lead Lab community. Multi-tenant architecture is not needed.

## Delivery Gates

### Gate 1: Environment Ready

Due August 20.

Pass conditions:

- Supported runtime and database confirmed
- Development and staging environments available
- HTTPS approach confirmed
- Backup location confirmed
- Technical lead and IT operator assigned

If the environment cannot be confirmed, the custom-app schedule is not credible.

### Gate 2: Vertical Slice Works

Due August 23.

Pass conditions:

- Participant can self-register as a pending account
- Administrator can approve a pending participant after the target-state verification gate is satisfied
- Participant can log in
- Unauthenticated visitor cannot see content
- Administrator can publish a lesson
- Participant can play its video
- Participant can download a protected file
- Administrator can revoke participant access
- App is deployed to staging

Failure triggers a scope and launch review.

### Gate 3: Feature Complete

Due September 2.

All launch-scope features must work on staging. No new features enter the launch scope after this date.

### Gate 4: Launch Decision

Due September 6.

Launch only when:

- No critical security or access defects remain
- Participant testing passes
- Required program content is available
- Backup and restore are verified
- IT support procedures are ready

Otherwise, continue using SharePoint for the September program.

## Security Requirements

- Hash passwords using the framework's approved password system.
- Require users to change temporary passwords.
- Enforce permissions on the server, not only in the interface.
- Block private files from direct public URLs.
- Validate file type and size.
- Protect forms against CSRF.
- Rate-limit login attempts.
- Require email verification and a working mail transport before participant use; the local development bypass is not a launch control.
- Record important administrative actions.
- Apply HTTPS before participant use.
- Back up the database and uploaded files.
- Test one full restoration before launch.
- Provide a process for disabling participant accounts.

YouTube links cannot be made fully secret. The project must accept that authenticated participants may discover or share an embedded video URL.

## Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Requester / Product owner | Approve scope, priorities, and acceptance |
| Technical lead | Architecture, code review, integration, and release |
| Development team | Build and test the application |
| IT team | Server, database, HTTPS, backups, monitoring, and incidents |
| Media team | Supply videos, session information, and materials |
| Test participants | Test realistic member workflows |
| LeadLab Director | Final launch approval |

At least one developer must work on the app as a primary assignment. Part-time development without protected delivery time makes the deadline high risk.

## Acceptance Criteria

The application is ready when:

1. Unapproved visitors cannot access community content or files.
2. Administrators can approve, disable, restore, and manage participants.
3. Participants can create posts and comments.
4. Moderators can manage inappropriate content.
5. Administrators can publish courses, lessons, videos, and materials, and open the Classroom recordings page from the dashboard.
6. Participants can search and filter sessions.
7. Participants can view scheduled events.
8. The application works on desktop, tablet, and mobile.
9. Required September program content is loaded.
10. Database and file restoration has been tested.
11. No critical defects remain.
12. The LeadLab Director provides final approval.

## Fallback Plan

SharePoint remains operational until after the program.

Use SharePoint for launch if:

- The vertical slice fails by August 23.
- Core features are incomplete by September 2.
- Security or private-access testing fails.
- Required content cannot be loaded by September 5.
- Production hosting is not ready by September 7.

The incomplete application can continue after the program without forcing an unsafe launch.

## Required Project Changes

After approval, the project should formally record the direction change and:

- Supersede `D-01 (platform replacing SharePoint: self-hosted WordPress)`.
- Supersede `D-02 (participant access: native WordPress login)`.
- Revise `D-03 (maintenance ownership: WordPress and server)` to cover the application and server.
- Resolve `D-04 (video hosting approach)` as YouTube for MVP, with accepted URL-sharing risk.
- Replace `AL-02 (same features with no new features)` with the approved community-app MVP.
- Stop `ACT-01 (configure the WordPress staging theme)`.
- Replace the WordPress backlog with the delivery phases and gates above.

This proposed plan predates CHG-13 (Replace invite-only or administrator-created participant onboarding with participant self-registration and administrator approval) and CHG-14 (Temporarily bypass email verification and local verification-notification delivery in development). Current control records hold those approved updates; this reconciliation does not establish a schedule baseline or launch acceptance.
